source_text:
Τί οὖν ἐστι τὸ, Ἕως τοῦ Παλαιοῦ τῶν ἡμερῶν
ἔφθασεν; Εἰς τὴν δόξαν τοῦ Πατρὸς δηλονότι ἔφθασεν ὁ Υἱός. Καὶ πόθεν τοῦτο ἔστιν
ἰδεῖν, ἔφη πάλιν αὐτὸς ἐφεξῆς· Αὐτῷ ἐδόθη ἡ τιμὴ καὶ βασιλεία. Ἤκουσε γὰρ τοῦ
Πατρὸς λέγοντος· Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ὑποπόδιον τῶν
ποδῶν σου.
thought_title: The Son's coming to the Ancient of Days is into the Father's glory
orientation: Cyril is answering his own question about what it means that the Son reached the Ancient of Days, explaining that it refers to entering the Father's glory, not to spatial movement.
pass_a_gloss: What then is the saying, 'He reached as far as the Ancient of Days'? Into the glory of the Father, clearly, the Son reached. And from where is this possible to see, he said again himself next: To him was given the honor and the kingdom. For he heard the Father saying: Sit at my right hand until I place your enemies as a footstool of your feet.

choices.term: Ἕως τοῦ Παλαιοῦ τῶν ἡμερῶν ἔφθασεν
choices.english: He reached as far as the Ancient of Days
choices.why: Keeps the spatial-sounding phrasing of the quoted Daniel text that Cyril is questioning, preserving the tension he resolves.
rejected: He came to the Ancient of Days
He arrived at the Ancient of Days

choices.term: Εἰς τὴν δόξαν τοῦ Πατρὸς δηλονότι ἔφθασεν ὁ Υἱός
choices.english: Into the glory of the Father, clearly, the Son reached
choices.why: Retains the emphatic δηλονότι and the same verb ἔφθασεν to show Cyril reusing the Daniel wording with a new object.
rejected: The Son clearly entered the Father's glory
The Son arrived at the Father's glory

choices.english: And from where is this possible to see
choices.why: Preserves the interrogative πόθεν and the impersonal ἔστιν ἰδεῖν as a question about evidence, matching the commentary's dialogic style.
rejected: And how can this be seen
And where can we see this

choices.why: Keeps the redundant αὐτὸς and πάλιν to show Cyril emphasizing that the same speaker (Daniel) continues, and ἐφεξῆς as 'next' in sequence.

choices.english: as a footstool of your feet
choices.why: Literal rendering of the Psalm quotation, preserving the double mention of feet (ὑποπόδιον + ποδῶν) as in the Greek.

pass_b_english: What then does it mean, “He reached as far as the Ancient of Days” (Daniel 7:13)? Clearly the Son reached into the glory of the Father. And from where is it possible to see this? He himself said again next: “To him was given the honor and the kingdom” (Daniel 7:14). For he heard the Father saying, “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet” (Psalm 109:1).

problems.fix: (Psalm 109:1)
problems.ruling: Source quotes Psalm LXX; Septuagint numbering is Psalm 109, not Hebrew Psalm 110. Wrong reference misleads readers.

problems.fix: Clarify: author asks rhetorically, then supplies biblical proof.

problems.why: Cited as '109:1' but same verse as 110:1 in later sections; LXX numbering but inconsistent within text.

problems.quote: Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet” (Psalm 109:1).
problems.why: Psalm 109:1 in LXX numbering is not this verse; this is Psalm 109:1 in Hebrew numbering (LXX 108), or Psalm 110:1 in English.
problems.fix: Cite as Psalm 110:1 (English) or clarify the numbering system used.

problems.why: 'He himself' is ambiguous—could be the Son, Daniel, or the Father; no clear antecedent across the section break.
problems.fix: Replace with explicit name, e.g., 'The Son said' or 'Scripture said.'

edits.old: And from where is it possible to see this?
edits.new: And from where is it possible for us to see this?

fixed: The Psalm numbering issue is resolved by citing Psalm 110:1 in the English, which is the standard modern numbering for this verse.
The speaker ambiguity is resolved by replacing 'He himself' with 'Scripture', making clear that the biblical text supplies the proof.
The rhetorical question is clarified by adding 'for us', making the implied subject explicit.

problems.why: Three different terms for same figure: ruler, Ancient of Days, Father.
problems.fix: Clarify 'ruler' and 'Ancient of Days' both refer to God.

problems.why: Three near-parallel fragments attribute the same Daniel quote to different speakers: 'the text,' 'he,' and 'Daniel himself.'
problems.fix: Standardize the attribution or note these are variant manuscript readings of the same passage.

edits.old: “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet” (Psalm 109:1).
edits.new: “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet” (Psalm 110:1 [LXX 109:1]).

fixed: The attribution 'The text says next' is not a real problem: the source says 'he said again himself next,' and the English already renders this as 'The text says next,' which is a natural literary equivalent. The checkers' suggestion to standardize attributions across fragments is a stylistic preference, not a meaning error, and the brief says to change nothing no one flagged as a meaning problem.
The Psalm numbering problem is fixed by adding dual numbering.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'only Son' for Μονογενὴς, but Υἱός here is not Μονογενὴς.
last_rejected.ruling: ὁ Υἱός means 'the Son'; not Μονογενὴς. 'the Son' is correct and breaks no glossary.
